extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, UIC administrators, legislators, and administrative law practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and criteria for handling overpayments, recovery methods, write-offs, sanctions, appeals, communication, and procedural reforms for an unemployment insurance scheme to ensure fairness, proportionality, and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of tax reversal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission should consider ceasing to use tax reversal except where people consent to its use with a full understanding of the consequences flowing from their consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax reversal presents potential unfairness and harm and lacks specific legislative authorization in the Act; use only with informed consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recover net amounts only
rubrics_metrics.description: The obvious and fairest approach would be to recover net amounts only rather than gross amounts that place onus on recipients to recover tax credits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If UIC can negotiate tax reversal to recover net amounts indirectly, it should also negotiate recovery of tax deducted at source from the Department of National Revenue for its own account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict garnishment and Federal Court action
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of other recovery methods such as garnishment and Federal Court action should be restricted to situations where the person affected has a recognizable responsibility for the overpayment's existence and undue hardship will not be caused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal Court action should be more controlled; require Commission to justify use by showing person was 'at fault' and had been convicted under the Act or had admitted awareness of receipt of monies not entitled to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation periods must be absolute
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitation periods prescribed by the Act should be viewed as absolute and unalterable; the UIC should not seek ways to avoid their effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act prescribes three years normally, six years if fraud or misrepresentation; written repayment agreements and waivers of limitation periods of questionable validity should not be used to override statutory limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refine and publicize undue-hardship write-off criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria for write-off decisions for 'undue hardship' should be refined by the Commission and publicized; they should not be rigid nor allow mechanical application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria should encourage knowledgeable, reasonable exercise of discretion and allow flexibility and personal consideration of individual circumstances; minimal criteria include permanent restriction from full employment by disability or age.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and overpayment determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: An overpayment determination cannot by itself be appealed to a Board of referees and Umpires; these tribunals cannot vary the amount of an overpayment but can vary the decision on which it was based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards sometimes shape decisions to reduce appellant's repayment responsibility; special treatment should be provided for overpayments caused by UIC error or delay so appeal system is not used to counter UIC-caused over-recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider write-off before automatic recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of write-off because of undue hardship as a prerequisite to the use of automatic recovery methods would help reduce large overpayments coming before appellate tribunals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forcing officials early to consider impact of recovery would encourage more acceptable approaches to debtors; also merit to subjecting write-off decisions to scrutiny by Boards and Tribunal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide full information to overpayment 'debtors'
rubrics_metrics.description: Overpayment debtors must be given as much information from the outset as they need to understand rights and options available to them and to the UIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current communications are minimal and cryptic; letters should inform claimants what they can do, how to do it, partial recoupment possibilities, that immediate voluntary repayment could stop tax reversal, appeal rights, discretionary write-off power and criteria, and the range of collection methods and powers available to the UIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose use of commercial credit information and allow review
rubrics_metrics.description: People should be informed that the UIC uses commercial credit information agencies and be allowed to review the information the UIC uses to determine financial capacity to withstand compulsory recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimants are currently not uniformly informed nor allowed to review this information; transparency would improve fairness in evaluating susceptibility to garnishment, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain garnishment operation and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Claimants should be informed how UIC garnishment operates and the potential consequences (e.g., up to 30% of earnings deducted at source or reduction of bank account savings by up to one-half).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although many recipients do not read form letters carefully, the gravity of garnishment consequences warrants clear upfront explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate detailed overpayment communication into broader info improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: A detailed approach to meeting information inadequacy for overpayments should be integrated into the improvements concerning information suggested elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Chapter 9 recommendations for a holistic information strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions duality and need for safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: The sanctions system provides both administrative and criminal sanctions; while administrative penalties provide flexible and less cumbersome enforcement, the delegation of penalty power must be accompanied by procedural safeguards and avenues of recourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative authorities may impose penalties more uniformly and rapidly but risk arbitrariness; ensure procedural safeguards prior to imposition and recourse mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionality between violation and sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental criterion for choosing between criminal and administrative sanctions is that the effects of the sanctions be commensurate with the seriousness of the illegal actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider subjective mitigation and indirect social repercussions that might make sanctions excessive; avoid disproportionate punishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for mitigating circumstances, including financial insecurity
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines should specify which 'mitigating circumstances' warrant administrative rather than criminal action and should include the financial insecurity of the claimant and his dependents at time of violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current UIC Guidelines on penalties are unduly vague; flesh out mitigation factors and define mercy-type considerations to give Agents II clearer evaluation basis and possibly allow refraining from imposing any sanction in appropriate cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend sec.123 to permit due diligence defense and limit scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 123 should be amended to explicitly allow the accused to exonerate himself by producing evidence of due diligence and to limit the section's scope to violations of the Act (not the Regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec.123 presently lacks an element of intent and can criminalize minor regulatory breaches; amendment would avoid imparting criminal content to regulatory rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand administrative penalties to Regulations violations (money penalty)
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC should be given power to impose administrative monetary penalties for violations of the Regulations, with the violator able to exonerate himself by showing due diligence and the amount capped at $500.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties should be recoverable in the same way as sec.47 penalties; delegation should devolve to Agents II for claimants, and employer penalties should be imposed or approved at a higher managerial level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals avenues for criminal prosecutions and administrative penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision to prosecute carries no formal pre-decision avenue of appeal; administrative penalties may be contested before the Board of referees like other Agent II decisions, providing speed and efficiency as a guarantee against arbitrariness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If administrative penalties are expanded, claimants and employers should still enjoy Board review; pre-decision review machinery is generally not recommended in respect of BCO reports or penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-letter should remind of possible sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The form-letter summoning the claimant to a benefit control interview should remind him of the sanctions to which he may become liable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This was recommended in Chapter 11 and reiterated with regard to penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1. Publish a Claimant's Manual
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC publish a Claimant's Manual containing all general information of use to claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2. Intensify public information and education
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC intensify its effort to inform and educate the general public.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3. Develop employees' non-official language knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC exploit and develop to a greater extent its employees' knowledge of non-official languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4. Statutory duty to inform
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act spell out the UIC's duty to inform insured persons and their employers (new sec. 105 A).

rubrics_metrics.name: 5. Publish consolidated Act and Regulations text
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC publish the consolidated text of the Act and the Regulations, preferably as an appendix to the Claimant's Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6. Concentrate procedural provisions in separate part of Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedural provisions be concentrated in a separate part of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7. Compile detailed alphabetical index of Umpire decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC undertake the compilation of a detailed alphabetical index by subject for the decisions of the Umpire.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8. Duty to give reasons in the Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act spell out the UIC's duty to give reasons for its decisions (amendment of sec. 53, 54 and 57).

rubrics_metrics.name: 9. Form-letters should specify concrete application of legal rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC, in notifying claimants of its decisions by form-letters, specify in concrete terms how the legal rule applies to the claimant's situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10. Monitor standardization of chairman's opening statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC monitor the standardization of the content of the statements made by the chairman of the Board of referees at the beginning of the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11. Summon interested parties to hearings more often
rubrics_metrics.description: The chairmen of the Boards of referees and the Agents II make greater use of their power to summon interested parties to the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12. Employer Record of Employment deadline in Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The employer's duty to issue the Record of Employment within five days of the termination of employment be transposed into the Act, the time limit being set at ten days (present reg. 140).

rubrics_metrics.name: 13. Administrative penalties for employers failing to issue ROE
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act grant the UIC the power to impose administrative penalties on employers who fail to issue the Record of Employment (amendment of the present reg. 146).

rubrics_metrics.name: 14. Replace submission with standardized summary of the file
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission to the Board of referees be replaced by a summary of the file, with an expanded and standardized content (addition to the present reg. 179).

rubrics_metrics.name: 15. Time limits for compiling and communicating file summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC be required by the Act to compile the summary of the file within 14 days of the filing of the appeal, and to communicate it to the Board of referees at least 7 days prior to the hearing (addition to the present reg. 179).

rubrics_metrics.name: 16. Record proceedings before Board of referees
rubrics_metrics.description: The proceedings before the Board of referees be recorded on magnetic tape and transcribed in the event of an appeal from the Board's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: 17. Include criteria for 'reasonable interval' in the Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act contain the criteria for determining the 'reasonable interval' referred to in sec. 40 (addition to this section).

rubrics_metrics.name: 18. Report 'Medical Yardsticks' data in sickness decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: In its decisions concerning sickness benefits, the UIC report data derived from its 'Medical Yardsticks'.

rubrics_metrics.name: 19. Account for local labour market supply and demand
rubrics_metrics.description: In its evaluation of attempts to find employment, the UIC take into account statistics concerning both the supply of and demand for employment on the local market.

rubrics_metrics.name: 20. Continue decentralization of operations
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC continue the process of decentralizing its operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 21. Continue efforts to personalize service
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC continue its efforts to personalize its service.

rubrics_metrics.name: 22. Subject claimants to Active Job Search Program
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC make all claimants subject to the 'Active Job Search Program' beginning with the week preceding the expiry of the 'reasonable interval' referred to in sec. 40.

rubrics_metrics.name: 23. Amend French wording of sec.55(8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The French version of sec. 55(8) be amended so that it reproduces the wording adopted in S.O.R./75-67.

rubrics_metrics.name: 24. Examine requiring employers to register all job vacancies
rubrics_metrics.description: The possibility of requiring all employers to register all job vacancies with the CMCs be examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: 25. Remind claimants of sanctions when summoned to control interview
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC remind claimants of the existence of criminal and administrative sanctions when it summons them to a benefit control interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: 26. Automatic re-examination of claim on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act spell out the principle of automatic re-examination of a claim upon receipt of an appeal (addition to the present reg. 179).

rubrics_metrics.name: 27. Right to apply for Board hearing any time during appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act embody the right of the claimant and the employer to apply for a hearing before the Board of referees at any time between the filing of the appeal and the decision of the Board (amendment of the present reg. 180).

rubrics_metrics.name: 28. Allocate hearing time per presence of appellant
rubrics_metrics.description: When it compiles the rolls of hearings before the Board of referees, the UIC allow one hour for hearing an appeal when the appellant is present and half an hour for hearing an appeal when the appellant is not present.

rubrics_metrics.name: 29. Chairman's prior determination on new facts for re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act give the chairman of the Board of referees authority to make a prior determination as to the existence of new facts or other grounds which would justify the re-examination of a decision of the Board (addition to sec. 102).

rubrics_metrics.name: 30. Organize technical conference on litigation problems
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC organize a technical conference on the problems of litigation concerning unemployment insurance benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: 31. Decentralize data processing services
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC continue the process of decentralizing its data processing services.

rubrics_metrics.name: 32. Board of referees decide appeals within 45 days
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of referees be required under the Act to make a decision within forty-five days of the day the appeal is filed (amendment of the present reg. 182).

rubrics_metrics.name: 33. Reduce Tribunal appeal period to 45 days
rubrics_metrics.description: The period for appealing to the Tribunal from a decision of the Board of referees be reduced to forty-five days (amendment of sec. 98).

rubrics_metrics.name: 34. File notice of appeal at Tribunal office irrespective of appellant
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal against a decision of the Board of referees be filed at the office of the Tribunal, irrespective of the appellant (amendment of the present reg. 184).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35. UIC file appeal docket at Tribunal within 21 days
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC be required to file the appeal docket at the office of the Tribunal within twenty-one days from the filing of the appeal (amendment of the present reg. 184).

rubrics_metrics.name: 36. Tribunal to give decision within 90 days
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribunal be required under the Act to give its decision within ninety days of the day the appeal is filed (amendment of the present reg. 186).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37. Equal rights of appeal and leave for unanimous Board decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: All appellants have the same rights of appeal to the Tribunal and all appeals against a unanimous decision of the Board of referees be subject to leave from the Tribunal (new sec. 95).

rubrics_metrics.name: 38. Boards sit off UIC premises
rubrics_metrics.description: The Boards of referees sit elsewhere than on the premises of the UIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: 39. Emphasize local knowledge in selecting chairmen
rubrics_metrics.description: Special emphasis be laid, in the selection of chairmen for Boards of referees, on knowledge of local conditions and prevailing social problems, and of the social security system.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40. Include at least one female member for women's appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC ensure that the Board of referees includes at least one female member when hearing an appeal filed by a woman.

rubrics_metrics.name: 41. Automatic dismissal for non-attendance without justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC automatically dismiss members of the Boards of referees after they have refused to sit on three consecutive occasions without sufficient justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: 42. Establish independent Federal Social Security Tribunal
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation be passed establishing the Federal Social Security Tribunal as an administrative tribunal independent of the UIC, consisting of at least three members with a variety of qualifications, including a chairman with legal training; and that the Unemployment Insurance Act confer on this Tribunal the appeal jurisdiction currently exercised by the Umpire (new sec. 92).

rubrics_metrics.name: 43. Tribunal chairman authority and leave decisions timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act confer on the chairman of the Tribunal the authority currently exercised by the chairman of the Board of referees with regard to leave to appeal; set the period for filing an application for leave to appeal at fifteen days from the day of the Board decision; and require the chairman to decide on the application within fifteen days (new sec. 96).

rubrics_metrics.name: 44. Limit judicial review by Federal Court
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicial review by the Federal Court be limited to the 'application to review and set aside' referred to in sec. 28 of the Federal Court Act (amendment of sec. 100).

rubrics_metrics.name: 45. Delegate procedural regulation-making to the Tribunal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act delegate to the Tribunal the power to make regulations concerning the procedure before the Board of referees, the formalities of appeal to the Tribunal and of application for leave to appeal — new sec. 92A and amendment of sec. 58(f) and 91(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: 46. Tribunal supervise and train Boards of referees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribunal be responsible for the supervision and training of the Boards of referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: 47. Tribunal publish collection of its decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribunal be responsible for publishing a collection of its decisions (amendment of reg. 186).

rubrics_metrics.name: 48. Bring suspensive effect of Tribunal appeals into the Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The suspensive effect of the appeal to the Tribunal be brought entirely within the purview of the Act (incorporation of reg. 167 into sec. 103).

rubrics_metrics.name: 49. Right to a hearing before the Tribunal in the Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act embody the right of the parties to a hearing before the Tribunal (amendment of the present reg. 185).

rubrics_metrics.name: 50. Right to apply for Tribunal hearing within 15 days
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act embody the right of the parties to apply to the Tribunal for a hearing within fifteen days of the day on which the docket is filed (amendment of the present reg. 185).

rubrics_metrics.name: 51. Tribunal indicate reasons for its decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribunal be required under the Act to indicate the reasons for its decisions (amendment of the present reg. 186).

rubrics_metrics.name: 52. Tribunal jurisdiction over other social security schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislation establishing the various social security schemes (unemployment insurance, CPP, family allowances, old age security) confer on the Tribunal appeal jurisdiction over litigation concerning contributions to and benefits from these schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 53. Publish a Manual of Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribunal publish a Manual of Procedure for the guidance of the Boards of referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: 54. Publish joint synopsis of substantive provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribunal and the UIC publish jointly, for the guidance of the Boards of referees, a synopsis of the substantive provisions of the scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: 55. Ensure hearing frequency for chairmen and members
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC ensure that the chairmen of the Boards of referees sit approximately twenty-five times a year and the members of the Boards approximately twenty times a year.
